value.description:
List of issued building permits from the City of Edmonton - Urban Planning & Economy Department for the public to do construction or maintenance on a structure located in the City. Note - All records start from January 1, 2009.
Please note : the decision was made to not release applicant information on this dataset as it was seen as a potential privacy issue. For instance, if a high profile member of the public were to apply for a permit, their name (and consequently address) would show up on this table and become easily searchable by the public.  We viewed this as a potential issue and decided to publish the dataset without applicant information.

Also Note: The General Building Permits dataset now includes an "Occupancy Date" to indicate when a building has met the requirements for use or habitation. 
- Residential: Permits finalized on or after January 1, 2022.
- Non-Residential: Permits completed on or after January 1, 2024, only if an occupancy record exists.
- Historical Data: Records before these dates are blank for accuracy, or if no permit was required.
- Usage: For trend analysis only; not a legal confirmation of occupancy for property transactions.

post.description: Any question that needs actual records from a Edmonton Open Data dataset. Get the 4x4 id from `datasets` and the column field names from `dataset` first. Use `row_count` to size a query before paging.

cursor.description: Row offset to start from: the `next_cursor` of the previous page. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,12}$.

dataset_id.description: 4x4 id (for example `24uj-dj8v`) or a data.edmonton.ca URL containing it.

filters.description: Bare equality filters sent as `field=value` query parameters (for example {"job_category": "Commercial Final"}); keys must be column field names, values strings.

limit.description:
Rows per page. The portal caps a request at 50000; wide datasets with geometry should use far less.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 50000; default 100.

order.description: SoQL $order, for example `issue_date DESC` or `count(*) DESC`. Default `:id` when no `group` is given.

q.description: SoQL $q full-text search across all text columns.

select.description: SoQL $select, for example `address,construction_value` or `job_category,count(*)`. Default: all columns.

where.description: SoQL $where, for example `address like '%86 STREET NW'`, `issue_date between '2026-09-01T00:00:00' and '2026-09-30T23:59:59'`, `within_circle(geometry_point,53.5449,-113.4885,200)`.

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
Query rows of any Edmonton Open Data dataset through the SODA 2.1 endpoint https://data.edmonton.ca/resource/<4x4>.json with SoQL: `select` (columns, aggregates such as count(*)), `where` (SoQL predicates incl. like, between, intersects(geometry,'POINT(lon lat)'), within_circle(point, lat, lon, meters), within_box), `order`, `group`, `q` (full text) and `filters` (bare field=value equality parameters), paged with `limit` (1-50000, default 100) and `cursor` (row offset). Without `order` (and without `group`) the program orders by the row id `:id` so pages are stable. Numbers stay strings as published. Rows come back exactly as published: numbers and dates are strings, geometry is GeoJSON; `columns` lists the returned field names and Socrata types from the X-SODA2-Fields/Types headers. An unknown dataset id is not_found; a SoQL error (unknown column, bad syntax) is invalid_input carrying the portal's message; an empty page is a successful result with count 0.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `rows` as the primary payload key.

The provider does not publish a field list for this tool.

These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

default.description: Error response; upstream passthrough responses may use provider formats
